title: A sudden brief rally, clarity, or energy before death

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
The record must not be used to diagnose, time, or manage a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, and emergency decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: After decline, confusion, or unresponsiveness, a dying person may briefly seem clearer, more energetic, hungry, conversational, or able to say goodbye; family may hope this means recovery.

content_layers.observation_text: Public sources describe a brief return of clarity, awareness, speech, or energy before death in some cases, while warning that this does not necessarily mean recovery.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Cleveland Clinic, Marie Curie, and healthdirect support a cautious record on terminal lucidity/rally as a possible near-death phenomenon rather than a universal stage.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This record needs tenderness because it creates whiplash: the person returns and then is gone. DeathVocab should preserve both the gift and the injury of the rally.

what_this_is_not: not a promise that the person will rally
not a cause for stopping plans or care without clinical advice
not evidence that the person chose death
uncertainties: The record needs dementia-specific, cancer-specific, and family testimony before becoming more textured.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should explain that rallies can happen and can be precious, but they should not be treated as reliable recovery signs.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect how clinicians prepare families without stealing hope or giving false hope.
language_notes: The word “rally” may imply improvement; pair with “brief” and “near-death” caveats.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the v2 witnessed-moment schema. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical safety review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent or worried readers to qualified local support.
